vehicle.mass_note: Measured with setup wheel adapters, 75kg driver, 35kg fuel. Adapters cancel in ratios.

corner_weights.note: RR calculated: total - FL - FR - RL. Measured on setup patch including adapters.

vehicle.yaw_inertia_note: Estimated from Iz = m*a*b bicycle model approximation. Error ~10-20%. Replace with homologation value when available.
vehicle.steering_ratio_note: Read from steering ratio lookup table at centre wheel travel and zero steering stroke. Treated as constant at Level 1.
vehicle.cog_note: Derived from static weight distribution. a = L * rear_fraction, b = L * front_fraction.
vehicle.cog_height_note: Reviewer-supplied order-of-magnitude placeholder, NOT sourced, replace with team figure.
vehicle.track_width_note: Reviewer-supplied order-of-magnitude placeholder, NOT sourced, replace with team figure.

aero.air_density_note: ISA sea-level standard value, a standard reference constant (Level 1 by convention, like wheelbase_m). It would only move with a session weather correction, which is not implemented.
aero.lift_coeff_sign_convention: cl < 0 means downforce, cl > 0 means lift (standard aerodynamic Cl sign, not a downforce-positive convention); verified computationally against estimate_vertical_loads. The first real Cl entry must be negative.
aero.lift_coeff_note: Placeholder 0.0, Level 1: the config aero term is zero at every speed, so Fz reduces to the static + longitudinal estimate -- an underestimate of both axle loads at speed, not a front/rear balance error. Sign: standard aerodynamic convention, Cl < 0 = downforce, as in the chair formula fz_aero = -0.5 rho v^2 A Cl (after the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal)). A first real (negative) Cl must be checked on a high-speed straight: the axle-load sum must rise with v^2.
aero.cross_track_area_note: Frontal area, Level 1, literature (cross_track_area_derived_from): used for drag with longitudinal_stiffness.drag_coeff. A is shared with the lift model, which stays at zero because lift_coeff = 0.
aero.cross_track_area_derived_from: 2026-10-21, author ruling (DECISIONS 'Drag adopted'): A = 2.0 m^2 -- Trzesniowski 2019 Gesamtfahrzeug [Trzesniowski.2019b] p. 257, Abb. 5.89 caption, generic race car with touring-car dimensions, A_V = 2.0 m^2; cross-check Katz 1995 [Katz.1995] Appendix 1 p. 264, Porsche 911 Carrera road car A = 1.78 m^2 (the GT3 R is wider). Pages verified by the reviewer. No team value exists. Limit: source values from about 1990.
aero.diff_cog_x_note: CoP-to-CoG longitudinal offset. Not sourced, inert while lift_coeff=0.0. 0.0 also has a standalone physical meaning if ever populated alone: aero centre of pressure coincides with CoG, i.e. no front/rear aero balance shift.

stability_estimation._comment_yaw_rate_unit: Unit yaw_rate_to_radps converts from (rpm: 2*pi/60 = 0.10472). csv_parser._assert_fixed_factor_units checks it against the file's declared sclu_yaw_rate unit; a mismatch stops the parse instead of scaling yaw rate by the wrong factor.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_window_floors: CS window floors: cs_min_window_s = 0.1 s, the chair's own value, unchanged. Tested 0.2 s against it on real data (100 Hz grid): same results on all 14 corners, no bootstrap difference -> no reason to deviate. Bootstrap spread measures precision, not closeness to the true tangent; floors chosen by direct validation.
stability_estimation.cs_min_window_s_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_cs_floor_candidate_validation.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22) + inspect_cs_duration_only_comparison.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22), 2026-09-02 -- see _comment_cs_window_floors. Exactly the chair's own literal default (10 samples @ their 100 Hz = 0.1s), zero deviation, now that the 100 Hz grid supplies the sample count that default always assumed. A 0.2s hypothesis (double the chair's value, motivated by an a priori 'this car's alpha comes from an ESTIMATED beta -- kinematic or EKF/auto-fit, a noisier Level 1-3 chain -- vs the chair's own MEASURED beta channel, so more averaging seemed plausible') was TESTED AND REJECTED, not just superseded: an isolated duration-only bootstrap (span held at 0.02 rad, cornering-only population) found 0.1s and 0.2s statistically indistinguishable at every tested phase length, and direct real-data validation confirmed the two floors reproduce the SAME worst-lap population almost exactly (identical negative-corner counts, same corners flagged, C4 rear even reads a stronger negative at 0.1s). The plausible-sounding physical story was not supported by either form of evidence gathered -- recorded honestly rather than left implied.
stability_estimation.cs_min_window_samples_floor_derived_from: Absolute floor protecting a much slower log (e.g. this project's own GT3 Paul Ricard census found 20 Hz) from deriving too few samples for a meaningful 2-parameter OLS fit: 0.2s*20Hz=4 samples would round below a robust minimum; floored at 5 (same magnitude as cs_phase_min_valid_samples's own robustness reasoning), mirroring modules.longitudinal_stiffness's own min_samples_floor precedent.
stability_estimation.cs_min_slip_angle_span_rad_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_cs_floor_candidate_validation.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22), 2026-09-02 -- see _comment_cs_window_floors. Rate-independent (alpha-domain, radians) -- no sample-rate correction applies. Reverted from attempt 2's falsified 0.01 rad back to 0.02 rad (the chair's own original span) after direct real-data validation; unaffected by the separate cs_min_window_s duration question (0.2s vs 0.1s) -- span was never the axis in question there.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_max_window_m: Locality cap for CS window growth, in track metres (state['s_m']), not samples -- same meaning in slow and fast corners. Natural window on corner samples: median 24.1 m front / 35.4 m rear; cap = 1.5 x rear median = 53 m; no corner lost at either floor (sizing and floor-validation scripts at git tag pre-prune-2026-10-22). The span floor, not min_window, sets the real window size. Limitation: some corner-to-corner gaps are < 53 m, so a window can bridge into a neighbour there. Floors not met within the cap -> NaN.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_phase_min_valid_samples: Per-phase CS_ratio median -> NaN below this many finite samples. 5 = smallest n where the median isn't just one or two extreme readings. Generic backstop; apex_3 handled by apex_region.
stability_estimation._comment_stab_phase_no_braking_floor_bar: entry_1_brake stability stat: same sample-count gate as CS (cs_phase_min_valid_samples), plus no signal if max brake_f_bar never exceeds this floor (no real braking). v3 log_pbrake_f at throttle > 90%: 32829 samples, p99 = 0 bar, one 6.03 bar transient (inspect_v3_brake_phase_stability.py, git tag pre-prune-2026-10-22). Real braking phases >= 13.6 bar. 3.0 bar sits between.
stability_estimation.cs_linear_slip_threshold_rad_derived_fro: diagnostics/inspect_cs_window_floor_derivation.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22), linear_region_end, 2026-09-02 (CS validity repair). Binned the session's own Fy-vs-alpha cloud (both axles, folded to a single sign via the tyre curve's expected odd symmetry, moving & non-kerb samples) with sliding 0.04-rad-wide windows (matched to the re-derived cs_min_slip_angle_span_rad, not an arbitrary narrow bin -- a narrower bin reproduces the same small-span sampling noise the N/span sweeps diagnosed) stepped by 0.005 rad, comparing each window's local slope against the near-origin reference window ([0,0.04) rad). Departure stays within +/-15% of the reference out to ~0.03 rad on both axles, then exceeds 10% and STAYS exceeded (not a single noisy crossing) from window leading edge 0.045 rad (front) / 0.035 rad (rear) onward, climbing to full sign reversal by ~0.08-0.09 rad -- the genuine nonlinear/saturation region. Value set at the more conservative (earlier-onset) axle's sustained-departure point, 0.035 rad, rounded down slightly to 0.03 rad for a safety margin against measurement noise; both axles' own curves are still flat (within a few % of the reference) at 0.03 rad.
stability_estimation._comment_grid_rate: Common grid = min(target_sample_rate_hz, slowest native rate of the fast CS channels: sclu_yaw_rate, log_asteer, log_acc_y, log_acc_z, lap_distance). On Dubai those are 100 Hz, ecu_speed 50 Hz (diagnostics/inspect_native_channel_rates.py); ecu_speed upsampled linearly (inertia-limited). Below min_sample_rate_hz -> refused, naming the binding channel; exactly 50 Hz -> runs, status 'channel-limited'. Windows are durations converted at the grid rate (kerb_dilation_s, kerb_smear_grade_s, cs_min_window_s, nis_gate.nis_window_s, yaw_stability_accel_window_s); the EKF Q is scaled to the grid step (tyre_fit_auto.q_reference_rate_hz). Known limit: apex_half_window_samples is still a sample count (+/-0.05 s at 100 Hz).
stability_estimation._comment_sideslip_source: Which beta feeds Modules 4b/5. Default 'ekf_auto_pacejka' (per-session tyre fit, gated, kinematic fallback). 'kinematic' = estimate_sideslip, the universal fallback; any other value stops the run. Traces are valid under any source; verdict thresholds are calibrated for thresholds_calibrated_for_sideslip_source only -> [UNCAL] marker otherwise.
stability_estimation._comment_sideslip_source_auto_modes: 'ekf_auto_pacejka': fit this session's tyre curve (tyre_fit_auto), run the NIS gate, use the EKF's beta_with_fallback only if gate = pass/warn and the fit is not degenerate; else kinematic, recorded as fallback_used/fallback_reason. [UNCAL] fires when the active source or tyre_fit_mode differs from the classification calibration tags.
stability_estimation._comment_vertical_load_source: 'static' = estimate_vertical_loads' static/aero/transfer model. 'measured' = wheel_loads cascade (damper -> axle-total reconstruction -> static) for the Fz used by fy_norm and the tyre fit. No damper channels (e.g. Dubai) -> every corner invalid -> cascade returns static everywhere, identical by construction.
stability_estimation.vertical_load_source_derived_from: DEFAULT FLIPPED to 'measured' 2026-09-04 (user decision) -- verdict independence PROVEN, not assumed, before the flip: CS_ratio/stability (the only classification/verdict inputs) never receive fz as an argument at all (code-level: estimate_cornering_stiffness/estimate_yaw_moment_stability's own signatures) and both run BEFORE fz is computed in the pipeline; empirically confirmed on Dubai -- fz_f_N differed by up to 8591.8N between static and measured, but CS_ratio_f/CS_ratio_r/C_alpha_f/C_alpha_r/stability_observed_Nm_per_deg were BYTE-IDENTICAL. The flip therefore carries ZERO classification/verdict risk by construction -- it only changes fy_f_norm_N/fy_r_norm_N (display) and the Phase-2 diagnostic mu tyre-fit's own load input, both display/diagnostic quantities. [2026-10-20: no longer true under fit L, the default since 2026-10-20 -- the measured axle loads are an input of the tyre fit, the observer and the CS (Fy / Fz); the statement holds for the per_session path only.] tests/test_vertical_load_source_default.py confirms the live default is 'measured' and resolves correctly both with real damper channels present (measured cascade engages, every corner tier=damper) and without any (falls back automatically, numerically identical to an explicit 'static' run).
stability_estimation._comment_cs_apex_region: apex_3 = one instant +/- apex_half_window_samples (11 samples; one helper, stability_analysis.apex_instant_slice, for every consumer -- corner statistics and the tyre-fit h2 check) -- cannot clear the CS window floor. apex_region = +/- cs_apex_region_half_length_m around the apex position, used for apex_3 CS reads in classification. 25 m = half the ~20-40 m extent of the C4 CS dip -> inside one event, short of the next straight or corner.
stability_estimation._comment_yaw_stability: Module 5 estimator (yaw_stability.py), after the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal); values = the chair's defaults. Changing any of the six means re-deriving the classification thresholds.
stability_estimation.kerb_dilation_s_derived_from: Q-CAL-1 option 0, author ruling 2026-10-03 (neutral engineering, unit repair). Replaces kerb_dilation_samples = 5, which was set as 100 ms each side on the old fixed 50 Hz grid and silently ran as +/-50 ms after the grid moved to 100 Hz (formerly a known limit in _comment_grid_rate). Restores the calibrated +/-100 ms; samples = round(kerb_dilation_s x grid rate) at runtime, so the physical padding is the same at 50 and 100 Hz. Premise check: diagnostics/inspect_kerb_filter_decay.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22), thesis_notes 'Q-CAL-1 measurement'.
stability_estimation.kerb_smear_grade_s_derived_from: Q-CAL-1 option 4, author rulings 2026-10-03. Grade-zone width of the near_strike mark: a CS window [start, i) holding a sample within this time of a kerb-mask sample (outside the mask, either side), or a mask sample itself (R1, 2026-10-17), carries the mark. Marked samples are left out of the per-phase CS verdict statistics (since schema 12, 2026-10-05); the CS arrays keep them. The zone also bars a window from setting the CS linear reference (Fix 0, 2026-10-17) and is excluded from the tyre-fit base mask with the kerb mask (R6, 2026-10-17). [Corrected 2026-10-17 (R6 docs cycle): the text read 'Flag only -- no exclusion, no down-rank, no verdict change', the rule of 2026-10-03.] The 2 Hz zero-phase CS filter runs before the mask and spreads a strike into unmasked neighbours; diagnostics/inspect_kerb_filter_decay.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22) measured the Fy smear past the edge at p75 = 0.25 s (15 NBR + 2 Paul Ricard sessions) and the coincidence count shows the deep-CS enrichment ending there (rear ends ~250 ms; front 250-360 ms band adds only x1.7). GEOMETRY: that 0.25 s was measured from the OLD +/-50 ms mask edge; the restored +/-100 ms dilation (kerb_dilation_s) moves the edge out by 50 ms, so 0.20 s from the new edge keeps the same measured physical boundary. One value, both axles (no front/rear difference in the Fy smear). Tier B.

tyre_fit_auto._comment: Tunables for tyre_fit_auto.py (per-session Pacejka fit, fit L, with EKF validation). P0, beta_hard_bound and r_yaw_rate_interim_seed_var carried over unchanged from the retired Dugoff EKF block (git history); r_yaw_rate_interim_seed_var is used only in the interim run that derives R_ay first (R_ay fixed before R_yaw_rate). Q is computed per session (l_q_derived_from); the observer resets on the hard bound only. Sweep scales = the grid of the original R/Q sweep.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_q_reference_rate_hz: Reference rate of the per-step process-noise variances: fit L computes Q per session as a per-step variance at dt_ref = 1 / q_reference_rate_hz, and sideslip_ekf_pacejka scales it by q_reference_rate_hz / grid rate, i.e. dt / dt_ref (first-order discretisation of white process noise, variance grows with the step): factor 1 at 50 Hz, 0.5 at 100 Hz (same variance per second). A convention, not a tunable.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_l_observer: Fit L observer: process noise Q computed per session (held-over-step upper bound, l_q_derived_from); reset on the hard bound only.
tyre_fit_auto.l_q_derived_from: 2026-10-19, author ruling (observer finalisation, Q-UPPER adopted): fit-L Q is computed per session in tyre_fit_auto._q_upper_from_residual -- the held-over-step upper bound from the fit-L force residual (Level 2): residual of both axle fits on their shared population, front brought to the body frame with cos(delta), propagated sample-wise to beta_dot = (dFy_f + dFy_r) / (m Vx) and r_dot = (a dFy_f - b dFy_r) / Iz, per-step variance SD^2 dt_ref^2 at q_reference_rate_hz, diagonal (Villano et al. 2021 dynamic filter; Bechtloff ch. 5). Evidence: diagnostics/inspect_q_upper.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22) (hard-bound re-entries 1-4 vs 27-246 on the derive split, all gates pass); method reproduced from diagnostics/inspect_q_phys.py. The keys l_q_beta_var / l_q_yaw_rate_var are removed (no longer read). [Superseded text, kept: ~~2026-10-19, author ruling on Q-PHYS: copied unchanged from q_beta_var / q_yaw_rate_var, a documented Tier B parameter, NOT derived. Provenance: hand-set base (0.1 deg)^2 and (0.05 deg/s)^2 per step at 50 Hz, scaled by the beta / yaw-rate Q/R ratio 0.3162 of the WP-S5b sweep of the linear Kalman observer on the Dubai sample (diagnostics/sideslip_kalman_observer.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22), commit 4b1b548). Diagonal form after Villano et al. 2021 (Meccanica, sec. 3.2). Not derivable from the fit-L residual without a reference sideslip measurement: the residual at the kinematic slip angle is dominated by a common slip-angle error (diagnostics/inspect_q_phys.py; held-over-step values recorded there as a per-session upper bound). Tested, not tuned: varied from /10 to that upper bound in the final chain. [2026-10-19: 'tested, not tuned' superseded by a declared post-result reopen (DECISIONS.md 'Q-UPPER frame'); the upper bound is under test as the fit-L Q, values here unchanged until ruled.]~~]
tyre_fit_auto._comment_l_straights: Fit L only: the steering-defined straights on which the session's ay sensor noise is measured (R_ay floor, tyre_fit_auto._ay_noise_floor; modules/straights.py, the definition of diagnostics/inspect_kinematic_inputs.py steering_straights). Tier B segmentation, thresholds from steering and speed only.
tyre_fit_auto.l_straight_derived_from: 2026-10-07 method choices of diagnostics/inspect_kinematic_inputs.py (kinematic-integration input audit; 'not tuned to a result'), moved unchanged 2026-10-19: histogram bin for the straight-line steering centre, a_thr / r_thr = sigma factor x robust sigma of the straight peak, moving average before differentiating the steering angle, minimum duration = longest candidate leaving the given number of segments on every analysis lap.
tyre_fit_auto.fit_speed_window_pct_derived_from: 2026-10-04, author ruling (session Step 2). Speed window on the Pacejka FIT POPULATION only (all three fit modes; NIS sweep, gate and CS keep the base mask): keep samples with speed inside [p_lo, p_hi] of the speed of moving samples inside corner instances on analysis laps, per session (self-adapting; fixed km/h rejected because it would mis-fit a track with a different speed envelope). null = off. Same function as the chair tyre fit's speed-band union (drops the fastest, mostly straight-line, near-zero-slip stretches); FORCED ADAPTATION -- one window instead of four band curves because the EKF consumes one signed curve per axle; the edge values are vehicle parameterisation. Tested in Q-FIT-DECISIVE as variant SW: verdict NEUTRAL; ships by AUTHOR OVERRULE (chair-closeness; pooled deep CS<-1 tail -40 %). Reference values, Tier-1 sessions: 69-70 to 222-229 km/h, 89-93 % of the base mask retained, 95-97 % of samples with |alpha_f| >= 1 deg retained, 2.0-2.1 % of in-corner fit samples dropped (diagnostics/inspect_speed_bands.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22)). Derived km/h per session are recorded in the fit manifest (speed_window).
tyre_fit_auto._comment_fit_density_bin_rad: Fit L: inverse-density weights on the signed slip angle of the fit population, weight = 1 / (samples in the sample's bin). Tier B preprocessing implementing the even data distribution of Goblirsch et al. 2025 (their own method unspecified); the bin width is a resolution choice, not a literature value.
tyre_fit_auto.fit_density_bin_rad_derived_from: 2026-10-18, author ruling Q-FIT-LIT (bin width carried over from the Q-FIT-SIMPLE Pw / E0w variants, diagnostics/inspect_fit_simplification.py (script at tag pre-prune-2026-10-22)). Not tuned to data.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_fit_long_util_max: Fit L only (tyre_fit_mode literature_bounded): BRAKING samples (Fx_axle < 0) whose longitudinal utilisation |Fx_axle| / Fz_axle exceeds this value leave that axle's fit population (heavy braking); braking side only (Fx < 0), traction combined slip retained, sized by the friction circle (Pacejka 2006 p. 5). The pure-slip curve is fitted on near-pure-slip data (Farroni 2016 T.R.I.C.K. footnote 9 p. 824; Farroni et al. 2018 TRIP-ID pp. 6, 16-17); friction circle (Pacejka 2006 p. 5): at 0.3 the lateral capacity loss 1 - sqrt(1 - (0.3 / mu)^2) is about 2-2.5 % for mu 1.4-1.6. Fx from the Goblirsch et al. 2025 Eq. 9 split, measured Fz. The observer still runs on every sample (combined slip in the observer = outlook).
tyre_fit_auto.fit_long_util_max_derived_from: 2026-10-19, author ruling Q-FIT-LIT final implementation: friction-circle bound on the lateral capacity loss (about 2-2.5 % at mu 1.4-1.6). Not tuned to data. [2026-10-19, declared post-result clarification: braking side only (Fx < 0); traction combined slip retained, sized by the friction circle (Pacejka 2006 p. 5); the first version omitted the sign and also removed drive on the rear. Value unchanged.]
tyre_fit_auto._comment_mu_demo_percentile: Fit L only: mu per axle = this percentile of |Fy| / Fz on the axle's fit population (demonstrated utilisation, a stated LOWER bound of true friction). Tier B percentile, frozen before numbers (author ruling). Anchors: Farroni et al. 2018 TRIP-ID p. 5 (peak bounded to the maximum acquired forces); Acosta Reche et al. 2018 p. 1904 (conservative grip estimate); chair performance_analysis tooling (internal), mue_effective.
tyre_fit_auto.mu_demo_percentile_derived_from: 2026-10-19, author ruling (frozen before any number of the Q-CAPACITY conditional run). Not tuned to data.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_r_sweep_selection: Accuracy Level 1 calibration tunables (config default), Pacejka path (author ruling). R is selected on the ay NIS exceedance only: in [r_sweep_ay_band_low, r_sweep_ay_band_high], nearest the band centre, and only if that grid point's sign-check fraction reaches sign_check_marginal_fraction; otherwise the next-nearest in-band point; none -> r_sweep_default_ay_scale / r_sweep_default_yaw_scale with status at most 'marginal' (marginal_reason r_sweep_no_in_band / r_sweep_guard_fail). Derivation: full 25-point grid on Dubai, NBR-73-010-026-JDR and MLA-SE07_US-v2: the yaw exceedance floor is 0.211-0.393, far above any NIS band -- the yaw innovation is dominated by single-track model mismatch, not sensor noise, so yaw is logged but not selected on; ay reaches [0.03, 0.15] on all three, so the band applies to ay. Default R = the setting chosen on all three exports (ay x0.1, yaw x16). A nearest-overall pick is not used: it chose ay x1 / yaw x1 on Paul Ricard, where the sign check fell to 5/15.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_yaw_mismatch_ceiling: Accuracy Level 1 calibration tunable, Pacejka path only (author ruling). The NIS gross-miscalibration trigger (nis_gross_miscalibration_fraction) reads the ay exceedance only; the yaw exceedance is logged per fit and can at most cap the status at 'marginal' (marginal_reason yaw_mismatch_high) when it exceeds this ceiling -- it never makes a fit degenerate. The yaw NIS reflects single-track model mismatch, not noise calibration. Set well above the observed healthy yaw exceedance range (0.21-0.52 over the full R grid on Dubai, NBR-73-010-026-JDR and MLA-SE07_US-v2) so it flags only anomalous sessions.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_status: ok/marginal/degenerate boundaries (status block of tyre_fit_auto.fit_session_pacejka) -- a proposal, not yet reviewed.
tyre_fit_auto._comment_plausibility_gate: Tyre-curve plausibility gate inputs. min_alpha_span_deg: p1..p99 span of the fit's slip-angle data (excitation), read by the fit-L gate (tyre_fit_auto.plausibility_gate_l). stiffness_min_npr / stiffness_max_npr: linear axle stiffness band in N/rad (magnitudes after Bechtloff, Fig. 7.2), read as the CS reference band when the CS runs on Fy (kinematic source, or fit L degenerate before the axle loads exist).
tyre_fit_auto.mu_ceiling_edge_u_derived_from: 2026-10-24, author ruling (work order DEV-3 item 1). Tier B, data-derived: width of the marginal band above the physical mu ceiling (tyre_fit_auto.L_MU_CEILING 2.0, Pacejka 2006 sec. 1.2.1); fit-L gate: mu_demo in (2.0, 2.0 x (1 + u)] = (2.0, 2.195] -> status marginal, the EKF runs (same structure as the K edge zone); above -> degenerate. Value = p95 of the combined relative uncertainty of mu_demo on the samples that set it (|Fy / Fz| >= the axle's p99.5), 14 development sessions, both axles pooled (n 7062; pool p50 0.071, p99 0.106), two independent terms in quadrature: (a) a_y error from the unknown IMU position, 0.08 g per metre of offset (p95, PRODUCTION.md 'IMU position unknown'), offset ASSUMED 1 m (author's example value; no mounting position recorded), divided by the measured |a_y| (2 Hz) at those samples; (b) the event zero's per-wheel u_wheel_N (channels.json event_zero_entries, NBR_221), per axle sqrt(u_l^2 + u_r^2), relative to the axle load at those samples, 0 on files without an applied zero entry (Le Castellet 25 / 32). u is a relative uncertainty, so the edge is 2.0 x (1 + u) = 2.195 (author ruling 2026-10-24; supersedes the first reading 2.0 + u = 2.0975 of the same day, no session's status differs between the two). u scales linearly with the assumed IMU offset of 1 m (term (a) is proportional to it; position unknown, to be confirmed by the team). diagnostics/inspect_mu_uncertainty.py, results_mu_uncertainty_20261024/.
tyre_fit_auto.tyre_fit_mode_default_note: fit L (literature_bounded) is the only analysis path: observer with per-session Q (held-over-step upper bound), hard-bound-only reset, measured R floors; CS on Fy / Fz with reference band [5.5, 35] per rad; g2 zones (author ruling). The key stays so the [UNCAL] marker and the thresholds' calibration tag can compare it.

longitudinal_stiffness._comment: Axle Fx from the CoG longitudinal balance (longitudinal_forces.py), input to the fit-L axle split and the floor-event attributes: drag and rolling resistance. The block name is historical and kept for its readers.
longitudinal_stiffness.drag_coeff_note: Drag sourced, Level 1, literature: with vehicle.aero.cross_track_area_m2 = 2.0 the CoG longitudinal force gains 0.5 rho c_D A v^2 (c_D A = 1.0 m^2). A is shared with the lift model, which stays at zero because lift_coeff = 0.
longitudinal_stiffness.drag_coeff_derived_from: 2026-10-21, author ruling (DECISIONS 'Drag adopted'): c_D = 0.50 -- Katz 1995 [Katz.1995] Table 2.3 p. 50, production-based GT race cars, 1990/91 Mazda GTO c_D 0.51 / 0.48, midpoint. Page verified by the reviewer; Katz edition (PDF labelled 2003 vs bib 1995) to verify by the author. No team value exists. Limits: values from about 1990, a modern GT3 carries more downforce and likely more drag. Sensitivity (diagnostics/inspect_drag_sensitivity.py): at c_D A = 1.0 m^2 against 0, 2.2 % of corner verdicts (0.7 % of corner-phases) change, 3 of 57 front floor events disappear, rear K shifts < 0.5 / rad, no status or fallback change. Outlook: Level-2 session estimate from the power balance (Trzesniowski 2019 Gesamtfahrzeug [Trzesniowski.2019b] sec. 5.4, p. 238, Eq. 5.13, Tab. 5.5; verified by the reviewer 2026-10-22).
longitudinal_stiffness.rolling_resistance_coeff_note: NOT sourced, placeholder. Unlike cog_height_m/track_width_m (which cannot legitimately be zero for a real car), zero rolling resistance is a defensible first-order racing-speed approximation on its own (rolling resistance is one to two orders of magnitude below aero drag and traction/braking forces at racing speed for a slick tyre) -- not an invented Tier A magnitude, a documented simplification, same epistemic move as lift_coeff=0.0.

wheel_loads._comment: Per-wheel Fz from pushrod force and suspension travel (wheel_loads.py; Segers ch. 9/10). Level 4 per corner where log_dms_dam_* and log_susp_travel_* are both valid; static split (Level 1) as fallback per corner, never a whole-session switch.
wheel_loads.pushrod_offset_note: Level 1 default (zero). log_dms_dam_* is already logged in N (checked in the raw file header), so an offset here is a zero-load calibration from a static gauge check, not a unit conversion. No entry point exists yet (no UI field, no setup_data key), so the raw channel is trusted as zeroed; the straight-line total-load validation checks that assumption. Event-specific gauge zeros (e.g. NBR) are handled upstream by channels.json event_zero_entries, before the range gate.
wheel_loads.unsprung_mass_note: Level 1, not independently sourced: per-wheel unsprung mass (upright, hub, brake, wheel/tyre assembly, half-shaft share), typical order of magnitude for a GT3-class car. Feeds the unsprung-mass lateral-transfer term, which bypasses the damper/spring entirely (reacts through the upright/tyre contact directly) and must be added on top of the damper-derived sprung force, never folded into it.
wheel_loads.tyre_dynamic_radius_note: Level 1 ESTIMATE, not a measured dynamic (loaded) radius. Derived from the team-supplied STATIC tyre circumference (front 2140mm / rear 2210mm, itself flagged TODO-verify, no datasheet seen) via radius = circumference/(2*pi): front 2140/(2*pi)=340.6mm, rear 2210/(2*pi)=351.8mm. Dynamic (loaded, rolling) radius is normally a few percent smaller than static/free radius under load -- this approximation is NOT corrected for that effect. Used only for the unsprung-mass transfer arm h_u; listed here explicitly as an estimate needing a better source.
wheel_loads.roll_centre_note: Level 1 ESTIMATE. Read from config/car_data.json kinematic_variants_front/rear's own stated baseline_variant (FS15 front, RS25 rear) roll_center_mm column, converted mm->m -- NOT confirmed against which kinematic variant is actually fitted for the GT3_PRC_MLA-v3 session (no setup record identifies it). Used for the sprung-mass GEOMETRIC lateral-transfer term (the portion of roll-induced load transfer carried through the suspension linkage/roll axis rather than through spring compression) -- this is the only sprung-mass transfer component added on top of the damper-derived force; the ELASTIC portion is already present in the measured pushrod force itself and must not be added twice.
wheel_loads.arb_motion_ratio_approximation_note: Approximation (author-approved): no dedicated ARB-linkage motion ratio is digitised anywhere in car_data.json (only 'N/mm at drop link' rate tables plus a scalar ratio_to_wheel). modules/wheel_loads.py approximates the ARB's own travel-to-wheel motion ratio with the SAME damper motion_ratio_vs_wheel_travel value used for the pushrod force at that instant (axle-matched) -- an approximation, not a measured ARB kinematic curve, flagged per corner in the module's own docstring.
wheel_loads.arb_position_fallback_note: Level 1 fallback ARB blade position (1-7) used only when no per-corner session setup value (setup_parameters arb_fl/fr/rl/rr) is available for the file being analysed -- GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt carries no setup-sheet record. 4 sits inside setup_parameters.json arb_fl's own recorded typical_window (3-5), a reasonable mid-stiffness assumption, not a measurement of this session's actual ARB setting.
wheel_loads.bump_rubber_note: NEGLECTED (documented limitation, not modelled). No bump-rubber engagement detection or force contribution is included in this estimator -- a wheel deep enough into bump to contact its bump rubber will read an UNDER-estimated load (the rubber's own reaction force is invisible to this decomposition, only the main spring/damper and ARB paths are modelled). config/car_data.json's own bump_stop_curve (cellasto_20mm_40shore) exists but is not consumed here; a future upgrade could use log_susp_travel_* proximity to the bump-stop engagement point to flag (not correct) affected samples.
wheel_loads.aero_front_fraction_note: Level 1 estimate, car-specific but not an aero-balance measurement (wind tunnel / CFD). Front/rear split of the session-fitted aero coefficient c_session in modules.wheel_loads.estimate_session_corrected_axle_totals (c_session is a Level 2 session measurement; this fraction is its only unsourced part). Derived from per-corner damper data on v3: residual_N = a + b*v^2 fitted per corner on straight-line samples (|ax|, |ay| < 0.5) gives b_fl 0.178, b_fr 0.214, b_rl 0.604, b_rr 0.573 N/(m/s)^2 (R^2 0.56/0.61/0.91/0.91); front fraction = 0.392 / (0.392 + 1.177) = 0.25. Cross-check: Dubai's independent RL b = 0.611 vs v3 0.604. Left/right roll-transfer terms cancel in an axle total (+0.00 N) and the axle-total residual is uncorrelated with |ay| (+0.031 / -0.058), so the v^2 fit carries no roll-transfer effect. Single-car, two-session evidence; open with the team for wind-tunnel / CFD confirmation. Every reconstruction result reports the value used (aero_front_fraction key).
wheel_loads.plausibility_min_static_fraction_derived: 2026-10-24, author ruling (work order DEV-4 item 3). Tier B: downforce >= 0, margin covers measurement error. Session check of the damper path (wheel_loads.straight_line_plausibility): mean straight-line (moving, |ax|, |ay| < 0.5 m/s^2, the session-fit mask) damper axle total over the static weight m g; below this fraction the damper path is rejected for the session and the static split (Level 1) is used, flag and reason in the fit manifest (axle_load.damper_plausibility) and the UI status line. Observed dev range 1.092-1.297 (14 development sessions, best available, m 1356 kg); labelled outings 1.052-1.250 with their setup sheets (m 1403-1407 kg), PRC JST longrun 0.081 (gauges zeroed against another reference, DEV-2) -- the only failure. Nearest healthy session 0.25 above the bound, so no PENDING review. diagnostics/inspect_wheel_load_plausibility.py, results_wheel_load_plausibility_20261024/.
wheel_loads.dead_channel_std_max_travel_mm_derived_f: 2026-09-03: Sample_Dubai.txt's log_susp_travel_rr found frozen (std=0.101mm, range=3.03mm over the whole session) vs its own axle-mate log_susp_travel_rl (std=5.39mm) and every other travel channel checked on both real sessions (Dubai fl/fr/rl: 5.13/6.52/5.39mm; GT3_PRC_MLA-v3 fl/fr/rl/rr: 4.88/7.01/7.20/4.87mm) -- a real dead/disconnected sensor, not a quiet corner (this file's own log_dms_dam_rr force channel is NOT frozen, std=2031N, so the wheel itself is moving, only its travel POT is not). 1.0mm sits with wide margin above the frozen channel (~10x) and well below every real channel's own std (~5x), a gap-selected floor in the same style as this project's other frozen-value guards.
wheel_loads.dead_channel_std_max_force_N_derived_fro: 2026-09-03. No real frozen damper-force example has been observed yet (every log_dms_dam_* channel checked on both real sessions reads std 1489-2083N) -- this floor is set conservatively low (roughly 30-40x below the smallest real std seen) so it cannot false-flag a genuine but quiet corner, pending a real frozen-force case to calibrate against directly the way the travel floor above was. Same guard purpose: a channel logged 'valid' quality and sitting at a plausible constant value is still dead, and channel_quality_gates' own range check cannot see that (it checks the VALUE, not whether it varies).

corner_trace_display._comment: Plot-only: how far the corner trace window extends beyond the phase bracket, for approach and coast-out context. Clamped at the lap's own s range. Phase bands still cover the five phases only.
corner_trace_display.cs_ls_panel_y_range_note: Fixed y-range of the CS ratio panels in ui/views/corner_trace_dialog.py; numerically unstable windows would otherwise force an auto-range so wide that the meaningful 0..1 region collapses. Data-derived from CS_ratio's observed range on Dubai (kinematic sideslip; min -3.065 rear / -1.872 front) plus headroom. Display-only clip; out-of-range samples are not drawn.
corner_trace_display.default_laps_shown_note: Corner trace default: opened from an 'All laps' analysis, the fastest N valid laps of the corner start checked, the rest unchecked but available (a single-lap analysis shows that lap). Avoids overlapping colours on corners with many laps without limiting what can be shown. N = 5 stays well inside the 10-colour palette. Tier C UI default, not an analysis parameter.
corner_trace_display.kerb_gap_bridge_derived_from: display continuity only, 2026-09-30. Corner and lap trace windows draw a dashed, lighter linear bridge across NaN runs that contain kerb-flagged samples (CS_ratio f/r and stability panels); plot code path only, no analysis array reads or receives it.
corner_trace_display.kerb_exclusion_display_note: Kerb exclusion, ONE user-facing concept (author ruling). Plot-only switch for every CS trace, histogram and tyre-curve scatter in the trace dialogs, the figure exports and the diagnostics renders, so app and thesis figures agree: grey (default) = kerb-affected samples drawn grey (hollow in the tyre-curve scatter); exclude = left out of the plot; off = drawn like every other sample. Every view states one caption with the count. Kerb-affected = inside the kerb mask or carrying the estimator's grade mark (internal name near_strike, width stability_estimation.kerb_smear_grade_s). Presentation only: the estimator deletes nothing and no computed result changes.

cs_envelope._comment: Corner-trace cross-lap envelope (core/trace_display.cross_lap_envelope), drawn as two thin lines on the CS front / CS rear / stability panels over ALL analysis laps of the corner; the selected lap full-strength on top. Display only.
cs_envelope.percentiles_derived_from: Author ruling 2026-10-06 (app check): p10 / p90 rather than min / max -- one wild lap must not set the visual band.
cs_envelope.min_laps_derived_from: Display floor: fewer than 3 analysis laps at a grid point -> no band there (same floor as the earlier cross-lap pooling grid, git history).
cs_envelope.grid_m_derived_from: 1 m track-position step (same step as the earlier cross-lap pooling grid, git history).

classification._comment_thresholds_calibrated_for_tyre_: The tyre_fit_mode the CS thresholds were derived on (fit L). With sideslip_source ekf_auto_pacejka the [UNCAL] marker fires when the active tyre_fit_mode differs (stability_analysis.thresholds_calibrated; author ruling: thresholds encode the estimator).

setup_engine._comment: modules/setup_engine.py. Repetition rule (Tier B preprocessing): a corner-phase symptom counts when it appears in more than min_repeat_fraction of the corner's valid laps AND in at least min_repeat_laps laps. Session layer: share of corners with a counted symptom, always computed and reported; the session setup recommendation comes from session_vote, not from session_share_threshold.
setup_engine.repeat_derived_from: author ruling 2026-10-22 (D5: present in a majority of valid laps, minimum 2)
setup_engine.session_share_threshold_derived_from: author ruling 2026-10-22 (4e item 3): kept null -- the layer is computed and reported (per-lap cell shares without the majority rule, share of corners with a counted symptom), no session recommendation and no threshold set
setup_engine.damper_step_derived_from: team practice: dampers for race-weekend finetuning (Setup_change_overview); TE p. 292 larger steps = test-day advice. Registry adjustment_step 'fine' (1 click) over 'exploratory' (2 clicks); author ruling 2026-10-22 (4e item 2)

session_vote._comment: Session setup recommendation (Tier B aggregation rule): every counted corner symptom votes for its mechanical candidate rows (lever group, signed direction) with weight = severity_weight[severity] x k / n (k laps showing the symptom of the corner's n valid laps); votes of the same lever group in the opposite direction are subtracted (net support = support - opposition); net <= 0 is never recommended. Engineer layer: driver-only symptoms (|feedback| >= 4, no data support) vote with driver_only_weight x 1.

limit_events._comment: Event layer (modules/limit_events.py), display + record only: the floor events -- contiguous runs of CS below the pure-lateral floor -0.53 with measured attributes (limit_events.detect_floor_events; no bridging or minimum duration, only recurrence_radius_m applies); never a verdict or recommendation input.
limit_events.recurrence_radius_m_derived_from: Q-SPIKE-AUDIT frozen header (SITE_M, the Q-PAIRING radius, 2026-10-05): an event recurs when another analysis lap has an event of the same axle at the same corner with its minimum within this lap distance.

accuracy_levels._comment: Accuracy per quantity: 1 = config default, 2 = session measurement, 3 = logged sensor, 4 = lookup table. Per node: level (static default tier), source, capped_by ('chained-constant: <name>' = an L1 constant in its derivation; 'provenance-assumption: <name>' = an unverifiable assumption about the channel; null = neither). accuracy_resolution.py resolves leaf nodes (mass, corner_weights, steering_ratio) per outing; derived nodes cascade from capped_by -- pure (= input level) or bounded by method_ceiling (e.g. yaw_inertia's m*a*b). Other nodes stay at their static level regardless of cap.

steering_ratio.source: config default (vehicle.steering_ratio); dynamically resolves to Level 4 (car_data.json steering_ratio_table, manufacturer digitised) when that local-only file is present and the cap allows it -- modules/accuracy_resolution.py. At Level 4 the wheel angle is interpolated from the table's wheel-angle column (mean of both front wheels), not divided by its ratio column, which is the local slope (corrected 2026-10-04, schema 10). Parameterization, not a chair-comparison deviation: the constant was never a chair scientific position, it is this car's own mechanical steering geometry.

longitudinal_force_split.source: Fx fallback tier: m*ax + drag + rolling (estimate_longitudinal_forces), chair-identical construction (docs/literature/longitudinal_stiffness_estimator.py, internal); axle split by measured axle load in tyre_fit_auto (Goblirsch 2025, Eq. 9)
longitudinal_force_split.note: Drag sourced, Level 1, literature: drag_coeff 0.50 x cross_track_area_m2 2.0 = c_D A 1.0 m^2; rolling_resistance_coeff stays 0 (documented approximation). A is shared with the lift model, which stays at zero because lift_coeff = 0.

sideslip_angle.source: per-session EKF/Pacejka auto-fit, gated (modules/tyre_fit_auto.resolve_sideslip_beta, stability_estimation.sideslip_source='ekf_auto_pacejka', production default since 2026-09-01), falling back to kinematic integration + washout (estimate_sideslip) whenever modules/nis_gate.py verdicts 'fail' or the fit is 'degenerate'
sideslip_angle.note: GPS-course L3 path investigated (two iterations): NOT viable on this dataset - diagnosed scale-drift corrected and corroborated, remaining error not dominated by it; shelved pending denser anchor data (longer session / more straights). Still Level 1: the auto-fit is a per-session model fit, not a higher-tier measured/logged/lookup source: fallback path and gate outcome are recorded in the analysis payload (fallback_used/fallback_reason), never silent.

speed.capped_by: provenance-assumption: opaque ECU wheel-speed calibration (thesis_notes.md limitations register item 10)
speed.note: GPS speed cross-validation is diagnostic only; ecu_speed stays the production source and time anchor. Origin-regression scale factor k = 1.012 (ecu_speed ~1.2 % low vs GPS, tight across speed classes; slip not confirmed as the driver) -- a candidate rolling-radius correction. Applying k would be an estimator-input change (v feeds Modules 2-5 and the aero Fz term) and is not done.

yaw_rate.source: sclu_yaw_rate logged channel, exact rpm-to-radps unit conversion

steering_angle.source: log_asteer logged channel (steering-wheel angle), converted via the constant steering_ratio at Level 1 or the manufacturer wheel-angle map at Level 4 (pure cascade -- resolves to steering_ratio's own resolved level)

lateral_acc.source: log_acc_y logged channel, exact g-to-mps2 unit conversion

wheelbase_m.note: Fixed chassis dimension, known to design tolerance; not expected to move enough to justify a dedicated remeasurement -- kept at Level 1 by convention, not as a live upgrade target.

vertical_load_split.source: axle Fz static + aero + longitudinal-transfer decomposition (estimate_vertical_loads), chair-identical construction (docs/literature/data_handler.py, internal)

per_wheel_load_split.source: per-axle independent lateral-transfer split (estimate_vertical_loads), the chair's own construction (docs/literature/data_handler.py, internal) -- NOT the roll-stiffness apportionment scoped as a later DOMAIN IMPROVEMENT
per_wheel_load_split.note: Describes the static split only. With vertical_load_source = measured the level is per sample (vertical_load_source_per_sample): 'damper' = L4 (logged sensor + motion-ratio table); NBR damper loads carry an event zero entry (channels.json event_zero_entries) and are 'L4 with an L2 zero' (L4-rel, author ruling).

wheel_load_damper.source: damper/pushrod force + motion ratio + ARB + unsprung/geometric lateral-transfer decomposition (modules/wheel_loads.py), per corner, when log_dms_dam_* and log_susp_travel_* are both valid for that corner -- Segers ch. 9/10 method
wheel_load_damper.capped_by: chained-constant: wheel_loads.unsprung_mass_front/rear_kg, wheel_loads.tyre_dynamic_radius_front/rear_m, wheel_loads.roll_centre_front/rear_m, wheel_loads.pushrod_offset_*_N, car_data.json motion_ratio_vs_wheel_travel/arb tables
wheel_load_damper.note: Per corner, not per session: a corner whose damper or travel channel is missing or failed falls back to per_wheel_load_split's Level 1 static estimate for that corner alone, recorded per sample, never a silent session-wide substitution.

wheel_load_damper_reconstructed.source: quasi-static heave/pitch axle-total (vertical_load_split's own fz_f_N/fz_r_N) minus the real damper-measured axle-mate (modules/wheel_loads.py reconstruct_missing_corner), used ONLY where exactly one corner of an axle is damper-invalid and its mate is damper-valid -- Segers modal-decomposition method
wheel_load_damper_reconstructed.capped_by: chained-constant: vertical_load_split (cog_height_m, aero lift_coeff/cross_track_area_m2/diff_cog_x_m -- the axle-total half of this method), wheel_load_damper (the measured-mate half)
wheel_load_damper_reconstructed.note: Registered at Level 1 like per_wheel_load_split although it uses three real sensors: the registry records the provenance tier, not within-tier confidence, and the axle-total term carries the same Level-1 aero/cog-height placeholders. Cascade position: tried AFTER wheel_load_damper (Level 4, that corner's own sensor), BEFORE per_wheel_load_split (Level 1 static-only fallback) -- modules.wheel_loads.combine_with_reconstruction_and_fallback implements the three-tier order. LIMITATIONS (full detail in reconstruct_missing_corner's docstring): a single-wheel event unique to the reconstructed corner is invisible (the axle-total model has no road-input sensing); the warp/torsion mode ((FL+RR)-(FR+RL)) is unobservable with three sensors and a heave/pitch-only model; both corners of the same axle invalid at once falls through to per_wheel_load_split (one equation, two unknowns).

yaw_damping.source: D_psi = (C_alpha_f*l_f^2 + C_alpha_r*l_r^2)/v (modules/yaw_damping.py), with the effective stiffnesses taken from Module 4b's model-free measured local slopes (C_alpha_f/C_alpha_r), not from a tyre model -- no wheel load enters
yaw_damping.note: Werner Eq. 4.3 yaw-damping term: considered, not adopted; code removed (git history). Level kept as a registry entry.
yaw_damping.derived_from: Werner 2021 sec. 4.5.2 (Eqs. 4.3/4.4) and Milliken RCVD ch. 5 (sec. 5.7, Eq. 5.6); effective stiffness from logged Fy/alpha (Module 4b) instead of a tyre model, approved 2026-09-29.
